options.text: The reaction has completely stopped
The forward and reverse reactions are both occurring at the same rate
The concentrations of reactants and products are always equal
Only the forward reaction is happening

questions.explanation: Dynamic equilibrium occurs when the rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction. Both reactions continue to occur, but the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant.

questions.stem: Why is equilibrium described as 'dynamic' rather than 'static'?

options.text: Because the reaction vessel is moving
Because both forward and reverse reactions are still occurring, even though concentrations appear unchanged
Because the pressure keeps increasing
Because the temperature is constantly changing

questions.explanation: The equilibrium is 'dynamic' because reactions are still happening in both directions at the molecular level. It only appears static because the rates are equal, so there is no net change in concentrations.

questions.stem: Which condition is essential for a dynamic equilibrium to be established?

options.text: The reaction must be exothermic
A catalyst must be present
The reaction must take place in an open container
The reaction must be in a closed system

questions.explanation: Dynamic equilibrium can only be established in a closed system where no reactants or products can escape. This allows both the forward and reverse reactions to continue.

questions.stem: At dynamic equilibrium, what happens to the concentrations of reactants and products?

options.text: They constantly fluctuate up and down
They are always equal to each other
They all decrease to zero
They remain constant but are not necessarily equal

questions.explanation: At equilibrium, the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant over time, but they do not have to be equal. The position of equilibrium determines the ratio.

questions.stem: How do the rates of the forward and reverse reactions compare at equilibrium?

options.text: The forward rate is always faster
They are equal
The reverse rate is always faster
Both rates are zero

questions.explanation: At dynamic equilibrium, the rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction. This is why the concentrations remain constant even though both reactions continue.

questions.stem: If the position of equilibrium lies to the right, what does this mean?

options.text: The reaction has stopped
There are more reactants than products in the equilibrium mixture
There are more products than reactants in the equilibrium mixture
The reverse reaction is faster than the forward reaction

questions.explanation: When the position of equilibrium lies to the right, it means the equilibrium mixture contains a higher proportion of products compared to reactants.

questions.stem: What happens when a reversible reaction in a closed system first starts?

options.text: Equilibrium is reached immediately
The forward reaction is fast at first, the reverse reaction speeds up as products accumulate, until both rates become equal
Only the reverse reaction occurs
No reaction occurs until a catalyst is added

questions.explanation: Initially, only reactants are present so the forward reaction is fast. As products form, the reverse reaction begins and speeds up. Eventually the rates become equal and equilibrium is established.
